# Getting Started

## Launching Agent Studio

1. Login to the Demo Tenant  
2. Go to Cloudera AI   
3. Click on the [go01-aws-se-hol](https://ml-a12d17cb-372.go01-dem.ylcu-atmi.cloudera.site/)  
4. Go to the projects tab and make sure the scope is Public Projects  
   ![][image1]  
     
5. Find the project number assigned to you in the spreadsheet: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1is87k6K4nzrBjQbJd8Lt4RqNhcNBeX2JepXKgxc\_MGA/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1is87k6K4nzrBjQbJd8Lt4RqNhcNBeX2JepXKgxc_MGA/edit?usp=sharing)  
     
6. Click on on the project and then go to applications  
   ![][image2]  
     
7. Click on the agent studio application to launch agent studio

## Configuring Agent Studio

Agent Studio needs to be configured with at least one LLM. You can either connect a third party service like Anthropic or OpenAI or host your own model within the private garden of Cloudera AI Inference Service. 

For this lab we are going to connect to a model hosted in Cloudera AI Inference Service. 

1. In a new tab log into the demo tenant and go to Cloudera AI.  
     
2. Click on Model Endpoints to see all available endpoints served by all the various Inference Services running on the tenant. 

![][image3]

3. Click on the AgentHandsOn Endpoint and go to the Code Sample Tab. If the AgentHandsOn does not have any replicas available use the goes \- llama3 8b throughput. It will still work but will not be as reliable and may not use tools correctly as it is a much less powerful model.   
     
   Read the details above the Code Sample. You will see that this endpoint is currently configured with a LLama 3.3 70B parameter instruct model running on 4xNvidia L40s GPUs. Remember an endpoint \!= model. We could gracefully transition to a different model over time if we wanted to with the same endpoint.   
     
   Now read the code sample. This code sample shows you how to make inferences with Python. Notice that we use the OpenAI package to configure our call to the endpoint, despite this model being hosted in Cloudera AI. This is because Cloudera AI Inference Service is compatible with OpenAI’s open model inference protocol.   
     
   

4\. Copy the Model\_ID and the base\_url from the Code Sample. Store them somewhere safe. Also click on the Copy CDP Token and store it somewhere safe. 

5\. Go back to Agent Studio, go to the LLM tab and click Register New Model.

6\. Fill out the details of your model like below copying in the details you saved from Inference Service. The MODEL\_ID is the Model Identifier. The base\_url is the API BASE and the CDP Token is the API Key. 

7\. Wait for the model to validate and test the model using the built in test feature.
